newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bank deposits rise 10.2 percent in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bank deposits rise 10.2 percent in Nov.

text.p: Venezuelan commercial bank deposits rose 430 billion bolivars or 10.2 percent in November to 4.67 trillion bolivars from October's 4.24 trillion bolivar level, Softline consultants reported.

According to the firm's monthly round-up of 38 commercial banks, 34.1 percent of total deposits were saving deposits, 43.6 percent in current accounts, while fixed-term savings accounted for 19.4 percent.
On the asset side of banks' balance sheets, loan portfolios rose 179 billion bolivars, or 10.7 percent, to reach 1.86 trillion bolivars, or 30.2 percent of total bank assets.
However that figure was topped by investments in securities, which accounted for 41.4 percent of total bank assets.
Current loans accounted for 1.82 trillion bolivars of total loans, restructured loans 54.3 billion bolivars and contested loans 17.86 billion bolivars.
Provisions for bad loans stood at 178 billion bolivars at the end of November, Softline said.

Capitalization rates, the ratio of shareholders equity to total assets, stood at 13.01 percent in October. Meanwhile, the intermediation index, which describes total loans as a fraction of total deposits, stood at 36.41 percent, Softline reported.
